brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer at a corner of a cell
requirements.evidence: drawer:0#0,0#cut on piece:0,0,0;half-n at 0,0 south cut face

requirements.requirement: One spike at the very same corner of the same cell, touching the drawer
requirements.evidence: Configurator enforces SPIKE_CLASH: a junction with an existing drawer/bin on its cell cannot also host a spike at the identical junction. Attempt to add spike at junction [0,0|0,1|1,0] with drawer present was refused; offered alternative was spike at adjacent junction [0,1|1,0|1,1].

requirements.requirement: Drawer and spike touching at same corner
requirements.evidence: Built drawer at 0,0 and spike at 0,1|1,0|1,1 - the closest allowed: both touch cell 0,0 via its east/southeast corner area, sharing edges with neighboring bases 0,1 and 1,0, but separated by one cell diagonal as required by mesh collision rules. Parts: piece:0,0,0;half-n, piece:0,1,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:1,1,0;full enable adjacency.

finish.summary: Requested exact co-location is blocked by configurator collision rule SPIKE_CLASH. Demonstrated by placing half-n base with drawer then attempting spike at same 3-base junction – refused. Built nearest legal alternative: drawer on 0,0 half-n south face and spike at the next junction one cell northeast (0,1|1,0|1,1) which is the closest touching arrangement the system allows, verified with meshClash clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your corner pair — same cell, same corner — I'll lay it out now.

result.note: A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base (variant half-n, half-s, half-e or half-w) first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

A notch drawer stands in an empty cell beside two bases that touch each other: leave that cell empty, with two touching bases beside it. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
